text: You download a hundred and nine megabytes. About twenty-six of it is the game.
The rest is the engine carrying it.
Disco Ball Simulator 2000. You owe a million dollars and you own one disco ball.
So you swipe it, over and over, until the party pays it off.
A hundred and forty-six DLLs. Eighty megabytes. Three quarters of the download.
And the biggest file that isn't a DLL is Unity's own default resources.
That isn't a criticism. It's the floor — what a small game costs on a big engine.
Worth a dip. Every demo I open, I read the file list first.
